transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

I'm here because I just... I keep snapping at people. It's getting out of hand. Like, the other day at a safety meeting at work, I just started yelling at someone before I could even stop myself. I'm an inspector, and now the younger ones on the line, they act like they're scared to even ask me a question. I don't mean to be like this, but I just lose my temper so fast lately.
How often do you find yourself feeling irritable or angry, even when things aren’t particularly stressful or frustrating?

Well, like I just mentioned, it's happening all the time. Honestly, it feels like every day. I don't even need a real reason to get mad, I just... snap. That's why I brought up that safety meeting. I just started yelling before my brain could even catch up. It's constant enough that, like I said, those younger inspectors on the line are practically terrified to even come up to me now.
Can you think of any specific stressors or events in your life recently that might be contributing to these outbursts?

Well, it's not exactly a recent thing. It's actually been going on since a machinery accident we had at the plant. It happened right after they put us on an overnight schedule change, and... well, that was about two years and four months ago now. I've just been like this ever since that happened.
Since the accident and the schedule change, have you noticed yourself feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still do the things I normally do. I don't feel hopeless or sad or anything like that. It's just the anger, really. I just feel on edge and angry all the time, but I haven't lost interest in my regular stuff.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or were more easily agitated than usual—separate from the anger you've been describing?
No, I haven't had anything like that. I sleep fine when I'm not on the night shift, and my energy levels are just normal for me. It's really just the snapping and being on edge that's the problem.
Have you ever had times when you felt so good or so hyper that people around you noticed a change in your behavior or thought you were acting unusually?
No, I've never had anything like that happen. I don't get hyper or overly happy. I'm just regular... except for the anger. People haven't told me I'm acting unusually energetic or anything.
Since the accident, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, actually, I do. I go out of my way to not even walk past the inspection bay at work anymore. I just take a longer route so I don't have to see it. And... I really won't talk about the accident if I can help it. I just shut it down if someone brings it up. I even quit going to these industrial-history talks I used to really enjoy. They show all these pictures of old machinery, and it just... it sets me off now. So I just stay away.
Since the accident, have you had unwanted thoughts, memories, or flashbacks about it that come up even when you don't want them to?

Yeah, I do. It doesn't take much to trigger it, either. If I hear a clank from a cart at work, or... or just catch the smell of hot oil, it puts me right back in that bay. I end up seeing my coworker right by the machine, like it’s happening in front of me all over again. It just takes over my mind even when I'm trying to focus on something else.
Since the accident, have you found yourself being more jumpy or easily startled by things that wouldn’t have bothered you before?

Yeah, very much so. It's like I can't let my guard down at all. Even if I'm just sitting in the break room at work, or... or out at rehearsal, I'm always watching the doors. I'm constantly listening for any sudden machine noises, and I keep checking to see who's moving behind me. It's just... it's like my body won't believe I'm safe, no matter where I am.
Since the accident, have you noticed yourself feeling detached or distant from other people, or feeling numb to your emotions or surroundings?

No, not really. I mean, I still care about my friends and my family. I don't feel numb or anything like that. I'm just... really on edge all the time, like I was saying. But I still feel connected to the people in my life.
